evals.name: add-logging-to-new-service
evals.prompt:
I have a new Kotlin Spring Boot (Web MVC) service called `orders`. It has no logging at all yet. The request path is: `OrderController` handles `GET /orders/{id}` -> `OrderService.getOrder(id)` -> `OrderRepository.findById(id)` (returns null when the order does not exist, which the controller turns into a 404) -> `PricingClient.quote(id)` (an HTTP call to our pricing service). After a successful lookup the service enqueues `AuditJob.record(id)`. The OpenTelemetry Spring Boot starter is already on the classpath and exporting traces over OTLP.

Add logging to this service. Give me the dependencies to add, the complete logging configuration file, and the Kotlin code changes for OrderController, OrderService, OrderRepository and PricingClient. Our dev team tails stdout locally, but in production the platform scrapes stdout and wants JSON, and we also want the logs in the OTel pipeline next to the traces.
expectations: The logging configuration defines a human-readable console appender writing to stdout AND an OpenTelemetry log appender (e.g. io.opentelemetry.instrumentation.logback.appender.v1_0.OpenTelemetryAppender) both attached to the root logger, so the same log call feeds both; it does not replace the console appender with the OTel one or vice versa

Switching the console output to one-line JSON is controlled by a `LOG_FORMAT` environment variable (LOG_FORMAT=json), not by hand-editing the config per environment and not by a differently named switch
The JSON console output is one line per event and includes `trace_id` and `span_id` alongside the timestamp, level, message and fields
The human console pattern includes the trace ID (full or a short prefix such as the first 8 characters of `trace_id`) read from the MDC/context key named `trace_id`, not `traceId`
The code never copies trace_id or span_id into the MDC by hand; it relies on the OTel instrumentation to attach them

Log calls pass values as structured key-value fields (e.g. SLF4J fluent `addKeyValue("order.id", id)`), never via Kotlin string templates (`$id`), string concatenation, or String.format in the message

OrderService.getOrder emits exactly one INFO record per request on the success path (e.g. `order fetched` with `order.id`); any intermediate steps (lookup, pricing call, audit enqueue) are logged at DEBUG or not at all
The 404 (repository returns null) is not logged at ERROR; it is logged at DEBUG or not logged
Field names use dotted lowercase / OTel semantic-convention style (`order.id`, `user.id`, `error.type`), not camelCase like `orderId` or `userId`

Any failure path (e.g. PricingClient error) logs the exception object itself (so the stack trace is captured) at exactly one layer, rather than logging it in the client, the service and the controller

Dependencies are named by group and artifact only (e.g. ch.qos.logback:logback-classic, io.opentelemetry.instrumentation:opentelemetry-logback-appender-1.0) with no hard-coded version numbers in the answer
No println, System.out, printStackTrace, or Authorization header / token / cookie value appears anywhere in the proposed code or configuration

evals.name: review-pr-logging-violations
expectations: Flags `log.info("auth header {}", request.getHeader("Authorization"))` in OrderController as Critical, because it writes the caller's bearer credential into every request's log record
The fix for the Authorization line is to delete it outright (optionally relying on `user.id` once authentication resolves), not to mask, truncate, hash, or demote it to DEBUG

Flags that the same DataAccessException is logged three times (OrderRepository, OrderService, and OrderController) for one failure, and prescribes logging it once at the handling boundary (the controller that returns 500) while the repository and service only rethrow/wrap without logging
Tags the triple-logged exception finding Medium (exception logged at multiple layers), not Critical and not Low
Flags `log.info("order $id fetched for user $userId")` as interpolating values into the message and tags it Medium
The fix for the interpolated line keeps a stable message (e.g. `order fetched`) and passes the values as structured fields named `order.id` and `user.id` (not `userId`)

Reports the multi-line `OrderService ready` banner in the init block as a single finding (not split into several), explaining that one event becomes several records/fragments in a line-oriented pipeline, and prescribes a one-line message
Every finding carries an explicit severity tag (Critical, High, Medium, or Low)
The review does not mark the controller's single `log.atError().setCause(e)...` in the catch that returns 500 as a defect to remove; it is identified as the correct place to keep the one log
The output never cites a skill, guideline file, or `application-logging` by name as the authority for a finding; each finding is argued from its concrete consequence

evals.name: rewrite-unhelpful-log-line
expectations: The rewritten message states what failed and to what (e.g. `payment capture failed` with an `order.id` field), not a generic phrase like `error occurred` or `payment error`
The rewritten log call includes an `order.id` field passed as a structured argument (e.g. SLF4J `addKeyValue`), not interpolated into the message with a string template or concatenation
The rewritten log call includes an `error.type` field (e.g. the exception class name or the gateway's decline code)
The rewritten call passes the exception object itself (e.g. `setCause(e)` or as the throwable argument), not `e.message` concatenated into the text

Explicitly justifies the chosen level: because this catch swallows the exception and returns Declined, it is the handling boundary and must log at WARN or ERROR (not INFO or DEBUG), with a stated reason for which of the two
No card number (full, masked, last-four or otherwise), expiry, cardholder name, or the gateway charge token appears in the message or any field of the rewritten log call
The answer explicitly warns against logging the card number or gatewayToken (e.g. noting they must stay out even at DEBUG)
The rewritten call is a single-line event: no multi-line message and no object (like `card` or the gateway response) pretty-printed or toString()-ed into the message
